questions.stem: 提示：某高中調查全校學生對五項生活技能的看法，下圖顯示「想在學校學」以及認為自己「已經會」各項技能的學生比例（可複選）。請根據圖表，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖表內容，並比較「想學」與「已經會」差距最大與最小的技能；第二段評估學校是否有必要教這類生活技能，並提出一項你希望學校開設的課程或活動，說明具體做法。

tags.topic: 高中生想學的生活技能
高中生想學的生活技能

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有四個要求：第一段描述圖表，並比較「想學」與「已經會」差距最大與最小的技能；第二段評估學校是否有必要教生活技能，並提出一項課程或活動與具體做法。差距最大的是理財（想學 72%、已經會 12%），差距最小的是時間管理（45%、40%）；急救的差距也很大（64%、20%），想學簡單修繕的人最少（30%）。比例是可複選的結果，不要寫成「72% 的人選了理財，所以其他人沒選」。第二段的課程要寫出誰來教、何時上、怎麼做，不要只寫「學校應該開課」。
evidence: 比較「想學」與「已經會」差距最大與最小的技能
評估學校是否有必要教這類生活技能
提出一項你希望學校開設的課程或活動，說明具體做法
1.strategy_zh: 第一段用 gap 這個字把兩組數字串成對比；第二段可以用一次身邊的緊急狀況帶出急救或理財的重要，再提出一門課或一項活動的實際安排。
hints: 第一段：先說明圖表比較什麼，再寫差距最大（理財）與最小（時間管理）的技能，補一個對比
第二段前半：表明學校有必要教的理由，回應「家庭教就好」的看法
第二段後半：提出一門課或一項活動，寫出誰教、何時、怎麼做，最後寫出見解

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The chart shows what students at one high school think about five life skills. For each skill, it compares the percentage of students who want to learn it at school with the percentage who already know how to do it. Money management is the most popular skill, chosen by 72% of the students, but only 12% say they already know how to manage money. This gap is the largest of all. First aid comes second, with 64% wanting to learn it and only 20% able to do it. In contrast, the gap for time management is the smallest, because 45% want to learn it and 40% can already do it.
I think schools should teach these skills because we need them in daily life. Most of us study hard for tests, but few of us know how to plan a budget or help someone who is hurt. Last year, a classmate of mine fainted in the hallway, and nobody knew what to do until a teacher came. Therefore, I hope my school will offer a first aid course. For example, the school nurse could teach a class once a month during club time. Students could practice CPR on a training model and get a certificate at the end of the semester. In short, if every student learned these simple steps, our school would be a safer place for everyone.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
According to the survey, students at this school are eager to learn practical skills that few of them have ever been taught. Money management tops the wish list at 72%, yet only 12% of students believe they already know how to manage money. No other skill shows a wider gap. First aid follows a similar pattern: 64% hope to learn it, while just 20% feel prepared to handle an emergency. At the other end of the scale, time management produces the narrowest gap, with 45% wanting lessons and 40% already confident in their ability, perhaps because years of balancing homework and cram school have trained them. Cooking falls in between, and simple home repair attracts the least interest, at 30%. Taken together, the figures suggest that the skills students lack most are exactly the ones that rarely appear in the school curriculum.
In my view, schools are justified in teaching these skills, even though class time is already limited. Knowing how to budget or respond to an injury is crucial not only for students' own futures but also for the people around them. I realized this when my grandmother slipped in the kitchen last winter. I was the only one at home, and I stood frozen for several seconds before I remembered to call an ambulance. Some people argue that families, not schools, should pass on such knowledge, and parents certainly play a role. However, many parents work long hours, and not every family has someone trained in first aid, so leaving these lessons to chance means that some students will never learn them. For this reason, I would like my school to offer a one-semester elective called Skills for Real Life. Each month could focus on a single skill: students might plan a monthly budget on a spreadsheet, practice CPR with the school nurse, and cook a simple meal in the home economics room. As a final project, each team would plan a class trip within a fixed budget and justify every expense to their classmates. Such a course would turn anxious beginners into competent young adults. After all, exam scores soon fade from memory, but the ability to stay calm in an emergency or stretch a small budget lasts a lifetime.

paragraphs.function_zh: 描述數據＋比較：以「學生想學卻沒學過」為主軸，讀出理財差距最大、急救次之、時間管理差距最小，補上烹飪與修繕，最後歸納
paragraphs.topic_sentence: According to the survey, students at this school are eager to learn practical skills that few of them have ever been taught.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 第一段讀出差距最大、次大、最小的技能並補上烹飪與修繕，還推測原因與歸納；第二段有立場、影響他人的經驗、反方意見與反駁，以及每月一項技能、期末任務的選修課方案，結尾提出見解（內容 5）；兩段層次分明，轉承語功能多樣（組織 5）；分詞片語、not only…but also、讓步子句等句型多變且正確（文法句構 5）；用字精準（elective、spreadsheet、emergency），仍以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

top.comment_zh: 第一段依差距大小排列：理財 72%／12% 差距最大，急救次之，時間管理 45%／40% 差距最小並推測原因，再補烹飪與修繕，最後歸納；第二段表明學校應教的立場，以祖母滑倒時不知所措的經驗佐證，回應「應由家庭教」的反對意見後提出一學期的 Skills for Real Life 選修課，列出預算、CPR、烹飪與期末旅行預算專題等具體做法，結尾有見解。句構多變（with 獨立分詞、not only…but also、讓步子句、could／would 假設語氣），用字精準（tops the wish list、the narrowest gap、justified、competent）。未見錯誤。第一段結尾「這些技能很少出現在課程中」是圖表外的推論，篇幅也偏長，但不影響分數。

steady.comment_zh: 四項要求都有回應：第一段說明圖表比較什麼，指出理財差距最大、急救第二、時間管理差距最小並附數字；第二段主張學校應教，以同學在走廊昏倒無人會處理的經驗佐證，再提出由護理師在社團時間每月教一次 CPR、期末取得證書的急救課。缺點是第一段沒提烹飪與簡單修繕；評估只說「日常生活需要」，沒有回應反對意見，論證較單薄；the gap…is the smallest, because 45% want… 以 because 帶出數據略顯生硬；want to learn it、know how to 重複。未見文法、用字或標點錯誤。

top.comment_zh: 依差距大小讀出理財（72% 對 12%）、急救、時間管理（45% 對 40%），並補述烹飪與修繕；立場明確，用祖母跌倒的經驗、回應「應由家庭教」的反對意見，再提出整學期選修課、每月一項技能與期末專案的具體做法。句型多變，用字精準，未發現語言錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 讀出差距最大（理財）、次大（急救）與最小（時間管理）的數據；第二段立場明確，有同學昏倒的例子，並提出校護每月教一次 CPR 的具體做法。結構清楚，但理由與句型較簡單，learn 重複；未發現語言錯誤。
